q: The Battle of Plassey was fought in:
e: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey in 1757.

q: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
e: The INC was founded in December 1885 at Bombay.

q: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
e: W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session in Bombay in 1885.

q: Which Viceroy announced the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
e: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905; it was annulled in 1911.

q: The All India Muslim League was founded in:
e: The Muslim League was founded at Dhaka in 1906.

q: Who gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?
e: Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave this famous slogan.

q: Gandhiji called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after the:
e: Violence at Chauri Chaura in February 1922 led Gandhiji to withdraw the movement.

q: The Brahmo Samaj was founded by:
e: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj) in 1828.

q: Who founded the Arya Samaj?
e: Swami Dayanand founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 and gave the call 'Back to the Vedas'.

q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' is associated with:
e: Under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse, states without a natural heir were annexed.

q: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal (1793) was introduced by:
e: Cornwallis fixed land revenue permanently with the zamindars in 1793.

q: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
e: Gandhiji returned to India on 9 January 1915.

q: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at:
e: Sepoys at Meerut revolted on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi.

q: The 'Subsidiary Alliance' system was introduced by:
e: Lord Wellesley (1798-1805) used the Subsidiary Alliance to bring Indian states under British control.

q: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was related to:
e: Gandhiji led the Champaran movement in Bihar against forced indigo cultivation.

q: The Purna Swaraj resolution was passed at the 1929 Lahore session presided over by:
e: Nehru presided over the Lahore session that declared complete independence as the goal.

q: The women's regiment of the Azad Hind Fauj was named after:
e: Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Rani of Jhansi Regiment, led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.

q: Where was the headquarters of the Ghadar Party, set up in 1913?
e: The Ghadar Party, led by Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna, was based in San Francisco.

q: The 'Communal Award' of 1932 was announced by British Prime Minister:
e: Ramsay MacDonald announced separate electorates for minorities and depressed classes in 1932.

q: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between:
o: Mahatma Gandhi and M. A. Jinnah
Mahatma Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar
Jawaharlal Nehru and B. R. Ambedkar
e: The Poona Pact gave reserved seats to depressed classes in place of separate electorates.

q: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
e: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931, ending the first phase of Civil Disobedience.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal?
e: Warren Hastings became Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act of 1773.

q: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow?
e: Begum Hazrat Mahal of Awadh led the revolt at Lucknow.

q: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873 by:
e: Jyotirao Phule founded it to fight caste discrimination.

q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is popularly known as:
e: The 1909 Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims and is called the Morley-Minto Reforms.

q: Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced by which Act?
e: The 1919 Act divided provincial subjects into 'reserved' and 'transferred'.

q: Who headed the Cabinet Mission that came to India in 1946?
e: Pethick-Lawrence led the mission; Cripps and A. V. Alexander were its other members.

q: The Ilbert Bill controversy took place during the viceroyalty of:
e: The Ilbert Bill (1883) allowed Indian judges to try Europeans, which Europeans opposed.

q: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was passed during the time of:
e: Lord Lytton passed it to curb Indian-language newspapers; Ripon repealed it in 1882.

q: Who became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833?
e: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Bentinck was the first.
